Model $y_i = \beta_0 + x_i\beta_1 + \varepsilon_i$, $\varepsilon_i \sim N(0,\sigma^2)$, with data $X = (-5,-3,0,2,1)$, $Y = (-2,1,4,6,3)$. response.text:
## (1) Least-squares estimates and fitted line

For simple linear regression with an intercept,

\[
\hat\beta_1=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i-\bar x)(y_i-\bar y)}
{\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i-\bar x)^2},
\qquad
\hat\beta_0=\bar y-\hat\beta_1\bar x.
\]

Here

\[
\bar x=\frac{-5-3+0+2+1}{5}=-1,
\qquad
\bar y=\frac{-2+1+4+6+3}{5}=\frac{12}{5}=2.4.
\]

Compute

\[
S_{xx}=\sum (x_i-\bar x)^2=34,
\]

and

\[
S_{xy}=\sum (x_i-\bar x)(y_i-\bar y)=34.
\]

Thus

\[
\hat\beta_1=\frac{S_{xy}}{S_{xx}}=\frac{34}{34}=1,
\]

and

\[
\hat\beta_0=\bar y-\hat\beta_1\bar x=2.4-1(-1)=3.4.
\]

So the fitted regression line is

\[
\boxed{\hat y = 3.4+x.}
\]

The scatterplot consists of the points

\[
(-5,-2),\;(-3,1),\;(0,4),\;(2,6),\;(1,3),
\]

with fitted line \(\hat y=x+3.4\).

A schematic plot is:

```
 y
 6 |                          ● (2,6)
 5 |                       /
 4 |                 ● (0,4)
 3 |                    ● (1,3)
 2 |             /
 1 |        ● (-3,1)
 0 |      /
-1 |   /
-2 | ● (-5,-2)
    +--------------------------------
      -5   -4   -3   -2   -1    0    1    2
                         x
```

---

## (2) Fitted values \(\hat y_i\)

Using

\[
\hat y_i=3.4+x_i,
\]

we get:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
i & x_i & y_i & \hat y_i \\ \hline
1 & -5 & -2 & -1.6 \\
2 & -3 & 1 & 0.4 \\
3 & 0 & 4 & 3.4 \\
4 & 2 & 6 & 5.4 \\
5 & 1 & 3 & 4.4
\end{array}
\]

So

\[
\boxed{\hat y=(-1.6,\;0.4,\;3.4,\;5.4,\;4.4).}
\]

---

## (3) Residuals and residual plot

The residuals are

\[
e_i=y_i-\hat y_i.
\]

Thus:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c}
i & x_i & y_i & \hat y_i & e_i \\ \hline
1 & -5 & -2 & -1.6 & -0.4 \\
2 & -3 & 1 & 0.4 & 0.6 \\
3 & 0 & 4 & 3.4 & 0.6 \\
4 & 2 & 6 & 5.4 & 0.6 \\
5 & 1 & 3 & 4.4 & -1.4
\end{array}
\]

So

\[
\boxed{e=(-0.4,\;0.6,\;0.6,\;0.6,\;-1.4).}
\]

Residual plot points \((x_i,e_i)\) are

\[
(-5,-0.4),\;(-3,0.6),\;(0,0.6),\;(2,0.6),\;(1,-1.4).
\]

A schematic residual plot is:

```
 e
 1.0 |        ●          ●        ●
 0.0 |--------------------------------
-0.5 | ●
-1.0 |
-1.5 |                       ●
     +--------------------------------
       -5     -3      0      1      2
                         x
```

---

## (4) Compute \(R^2\)

We use

\[
R^2=1-\frac{\text{SSE}}{\text{SST}},
\]

where

\[
\text{SSE}=\sum e_i^2.
\]

Compute

\[
\text{SSE}=(-0.4)^2+(0.6)^2+(0.6)^2+(0.6)^2+(-1.4)^2.
\]

So

\[
\text{SSE}=0.16+0.36+0.36+0.36+1.96=3.2.
\]

Also

\[
\text{SST}=\sum (y_i-\bar y)^2=37.2.
\]

Therefore

\[
R^2=1-\frac{3.2}{37.2}
=1-\frac{16/5}{186/5}
=1-\frac{16}{186}
=\frac{85}{93}.
\]

Hence

\[
\boxed{R^2=\frac{85}{93}\approx 0.914.}
\]

So about \(91.4\%\) of the variation in \(Y\) is explained by the fitted linear regression on \(X\).
